encodingDesc.p: Printed small capitals transcribed in uppercase; ordinary line-wrap hyphenation joined explicitly; lexical hyphens, spelling, punctuation, brackets and printed footnote pointers retained. Raw digital HTML/XML, scan crops and source bytes remain recoverable. Comparisons may fold case and ae/æ; original source readings are retained without such folding.

normalization.p: Sentence-case presentation is an editorial layer, not a replacement transcription. Each choice retains the exact accepted 1856 text in orig and a case-only display in reg. Proper names, ligatures, punctuation, spelling, source pointers and Roman labels are preserved; common nouns are lowercased. Compiled-index CSS selects reg only, without altering other witnesses.

revisionDesc.change: Authorized human browser-review correction: one provenance note immediately below the index title; reversible sentence-case readings and left-aligned presentation. Original 1856 readings and existing structural identities remain intact.

div.head: Whiston’s chapter headings (compiled index)
div.note: Compiled from the chapter headings printed in the Auburn and Rochester edition of Whiston's translation (Alden & Beardsley, 1856). The arrangement as an index is editorial, not an original printed table of contents.

choice.orig: CONTAINING THE INTERVAL OF THIRTY-TWO YEARS.
choice.reg: Containing the interval of thirty-two years.

choice.orig: FROM THE DEATH OF QUEEN ALEXANDRA TO THE DEATH OF ANTIGONUS.
choice.reg: From the death of queen Alexandra to the death of Antigonus.

choice.orig: THE WAR BETWEEN ARISTOBULUS AND HYRCANUS ABOUT THE KINGDOM; AND HOW THEY MADE AN AGREEMENT THAT ARISTOBULUS SHOULD BE KING, AND HYRCANUS LIVE A PRIVATE LIFE: AS ALSO HOW HYRCANUS, A LITTLE AFTERWARDS, WAS PERSUADED BY ANTIPATER TO FLY TO ARETAS.
choice.reg: The war between Aristobulus and Hyrcanus about the kingdom; and how they made an agreement that Aristobulus should be king, and Hyrcanus live a private life: as also how Hyrcanus, a little afterwards, was persuaded by Antipater to fly to Aretas.

choice.orig: HOW ARETAS AND HYRCANUS MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST ARISTOBULUS, AND BESIEGED JERUSALEM; AND HOW SCAURUS THE ROMAN GENERAL RAISED THE SIEGE. CONCERNING THE DEATH OF ONIAS.
choice.reg: How Aretas and Hyrcanus made an expedition against Aristobulus, and besieged Jerusalem; and how Scaurus the Roman general raised the siege. Concerning the death of Onias.

choice.orig: HOW ARISTOBULUS AND HYRCANUS CAME TO POMPEY, IN ORDER TO ARGUE WHO OUGHT TO HAVE THE KINGDOM; AND HOW, UPON THE FLIGHT OF ARISTOBULUS TO THE FORTRESS ALEXANDRIUM, POMPEY LED HIS ARMY AGAINST HIM, AND ORDERED HIM TO DELIVER UP THE FORTRESSES WHEREOF HE WAS POSSESSED.
choice.reg: How Aristobulus and Hyrcanus came to Pompey, in order to argue who ought to have the kingdom; and how, upon the flight of Aristobulus to the fortress Alexandrium, Pompey led his army against him, and ordered him to deliver up the fortresses whereof he was possessed.

choice.orig: HOW POMPEY, WHEN THE CITIZENS OF JERUSALEM SHUT THEIR GATES AGAINST HIM, BESIEGED THE CITY, AND TOOK IT BY FORCE; AS ALSO WHAT OTHER THINGS HE DID IN JUDEA.
choice.reg: How Pompey, when the citizens of Jerusalem shut their gates against him, besieged the city, and took it by force; as also what other things he did in Judea.

choice.orig: HOW SCAURUS MADE A LEAGUE OF MUTUAL ASSISTANCE WITH ARETAS; AND WHAT GABINIUS DID IN JUDEA, AFTER HE HAD CONQUERED ALEXANDER, THE SON OF ARISTOBULUS.
choice.reg: How Scaurus made a league of mutual assistance with Aretas; and what Gabinius did in Judea, after he had conquered Alexander, the son of Aristobulus.

choice.orig: HOW GABINIUS CAUGHT ARISTOBULUS AFTER HE HAD FLED FROM ROME, AND SENT HIM BACK TO ROME AGAIN; AND HOW THE SAME GABINIUS, AS HE RETURNED OUT OF EGYPT, OVERCAME ALEXANDER AND THE NABATEANS IN BATTLE.
choice.reg: How Gabinius caught Aristobulus after he had fled from Rome, and sent him back to Rome again; and how the same Gabinius, as he returned out of Egypt, overcame Alexander and the Nabateans in battle.

choice.orig: HOW CRASSUS CAME INTO JUDEA, AND PILLAGED THE TEMPLE; AND THEN MARCHED AGAINST THE PARTHIANS, AND PERISHED, WITH HIS ARMY. ALSO HOW CASSIUS OBTAINED SYRIA, AND PUT A STOP TO THE PARTHIANS, AND THEN WENT UP TO JUDEA.
choice.reg: How Crassus came into Judea, and pillaged the temple; and then marched against the Parthians, and perished, with his army. Also how Cassius obtained Syria, and put a stop to the Parthians, and then went up to Judea.

choice.orig: THE JEWS BECOME CONFEDERATES WITH CÆSAR WHEN HE FOUGHT AGAINST EGYPT. THE GLORIOUS ACTIONS OF ANTIPATER, AND HIS FRIENDSHIP WITH CÆSAR. THE HONOURS WHICH THE JEWS RECEIVED FROM THE ROMANS AND ATHENIANS.
choice.reg: The Jews become confederates with Cæsar when he fought against Egypt. The glorious actions of Antipater, and his friendship with Cæsar. The honours which the Jews received from the Romans and Athenians.

choice.orig: HOW ANTIPATER COMMITTED THE CARE OF GALILEE TO HEROD, AND THAT OF JERUSALEM TO PHASAELUS; AS ALSO, HOW HEROD, UPON THE JEWS' ENVY AT ANTIPATER, WAS ACCUSED BEFORE HYRCANUS.
choice.reg: How Antipater committed the care of Galilee to Herod, and that of Jerusalem to Phasaelus; as also, how Herod, upon the Jews' envy at Antipater, was accused before Hyrcanus.

choice.orig: THE HONOURS THAT WERE PAID THE JEWS; AND THE LEAGUES THAT WERE MADE BY THE ROMANS, AND OTHER NATIONS, WITH THEM.
choice.reg: The honours that were paid the Jews; and the leagues that were made by the Romans, and other nations, with them.

choice.orig: HOW MARCUS† SUCCEEDED SEXTUS WHEN HE HAD BEEN SLAIN BY BASSUS'S TREACHERY, AND HOW, AFTER THE DEATH OF CÆSAR, CASSIUS CAME INTO SYRIA, AND DISTRESSED JUDEA; AS ALSO, HOW MALICHUS SLEW ANTIPATER, AND WAS HIMSELF SLAIN BY HEROD.
choice.reg: How Marcus† succeeded Sextus when he had been slain by Bassus's treachery, and how, after the death of Cæsar, Cassius came into Syria, and distressed Judea; as also, how Malichus slew Antipater, and was himself slain by Herod.

choice.orig: HEROD EJECTS ANTIGONUS, THE SON OF ARISTOBULUS, OUT OF JUDEA, AND GAINS THE FRIENDSHIP OF ANTONY, WHO WAS NOW COME INTO SYRIA, BY SENDING HIM MUCH MONEY; ON WHICH ACCOUNT HE WOULD NOT ADMIT OF THOSE THAT WOULD HAVE ACCUSED HEROD: AND WHAT IT WAS THAT ANTONY WROTE TO THE TYRIANS IN BEHALF OF THE JEWS.
choice.reg: Herod ejects Antigonus, the son of Aristobulus, out of Judea, and gains the friendship of Antony, who was now come into Syria, by sending him much money; on which account he would not admit of those that would have accused Herod: and what it was that Antony wrote to the Tyrians in behalf of the Jews.

choice.orig: HOW ANTONY MADE HEROD AND PHASAELUS TETRARCHS, AFTER THEY HAD BEEN ACCUSED TO NO PURPOSE; AND HOW THE PARTHIANS, WHEN THEY BROUGHT ANTIGONUS INTO JUDEA, TOOK HYRCANUS AND PHASAELUS CAPTIVES. HEROD'S FLIGHT; AND WHAT AFFLICTIONS HYRCANUS AND PHASAELUS ENDURED.
choice.reg: How Antony made Herod and Phasaelus tetrarchs, after they had been accused to no purpose; and how the Parthians, when they brought Antigonus into Judea, took Hyrcanus and Phasaelus captives. Herod's flight; and what afflictions Hyrcanus and Phasaelus endured.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD GOT AWAY FROM THE KING OF ARABIA, AND MADE HASTE TO GO INTO EGYPT, AND THENCE WENT IN HASTE ALSO TO ROME; AND HOW, BY PROMISING A GREAT DEAL OF MONEY TO ANTONY, HE OBTAINED OF THE SENATE AND OF CÆSAR TO BE MADE KING OF THE JEWS.
choice.reg: How Herod got away from the king of Arabia, and made haste to go into Egypt, and thence went in haste also to Rome; and how, by promising a great deal of money to Antony, he obtained of the senate and of Cæsar to be made king of the Jews.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD SAILED OUT OF ITALY TO JUDEA, AND FOUGHT WITH ANTIGONUS; AND WHAT OTHER THINGS HAPPENED IN JUDEA ABOUT THAT TIME.
choice.reg: How Herod sailed out of Italy to Judea, and fought with Antigonus; and what other things happened in Judea about that time.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD, WHEN HE HAD MARRIED MARIAMNE, TOOK JERUSALEM, WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF SOSIUS, BY FORCE; AND HOW THE GOVERNMENT OF THE ASAMONEANS WAS PUT AN END TO.
choice.reg: How Herod, when he had married Mariamne, took Jerusalem, with the assistance of Sosius, by force; and how the government of the Asamoneans was put an end to.
